column1: # p14 DPM {auto,high} interleaved benchmark, 2026-08-22, BIOS VRAM carve-out reduced 8 GB -> 1 GB.
# Matched A/B against dpm-results-iommu-off.tsv: same board, same DIMMs, same server, same
# harness, amd_iommu=off on both. The ONLY difference is the BIOS UMA frame-buffer size.
# WHY: with an 8 GB carve-out, VRAM ran 100% full (8157/8192 MiB) and the remaining ~36 GiB of
# the model spilled into GTT. VRAM is reached through the local aperture, GTT through the GART,
# and we had just measured that adding a translation layer to GTT (the IOMMU) cost 26%. The
# hypothesis was that moving MORE of the model into VRAM would help. It was tested in the
# opposite direction -- less VRAM, more GTT -- which is the same experiment.
# RESULT -- steady state, round 1 dropped, n=3:
#   arm    metric   UMA 8 GB   UMA 1 GB   delta
# CONCLUSION: VRAM-vs-GTT PLACEMENT IS NOT A LEVER ON THIS HARDWARE. Moving ~7 GiB of the model
# out of VRAM and into GTT changed nothing measurable -- every PP/TG delta is inside the
# run-to-run spread (sd ~5 on PP). Do not spend a BIOS trip and a reboot on this again.
# Makes sense in hindsight: with amd_iommu=off the remaining GART translation runs on the GPU's
# own page tables with large fragments, and VRAM and GTT are the same physical DDR5 at the same
# bandwidth. The IOMMU was an EXTRA layer on top of that; the GART itself is cheap.
# The -5 C at dpm-high is the one difference outside obvious noise, but it is not attributed:
# thermal history between two separate boots is the more likely explanation than the carve-out.
# PRACTICAL UPSHOT: keep the carve-out SMALL. Same throughput, and 7 GB returned to the OS
# (83 -> 90 GiB usable). 1 GB is the better setting.
# Provenance block below is emitted by bench-dpm.sh itself, added 2026-08-22 after a missing
# amd_iommu=off went unnoticed for a day and produced three wrong conclusions.
